```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("../../_shared/template/viscount_rmd_helpers.R")

sett_raw <- jsonlite::fromJSON("atlantic_west_equatoria_settlements.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)
summary_cache <- jsonlite::fromJSON("atlantic_west_equatoria_summary_cache.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)

all_keys <- names(sett_raw)
all_entries <- lapply(all_keys, function (k) {
  e <- sett_raw[[k]]
  e$key <- k
  e
})

fmt_eu_coord <- function (x) {
  s <- format(round(as.numeric(x), 2L), nsmall = 2L, trim = TRUE)
  gsub("\\.", ",", s)
}

interp_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  ord <- order(yrs)
  yrs <- yrs[ord]
  vals <- vals[ord]
  if (yr_num < yrs[1] || yr_num > yrs[length(yrs)]) return(NA_real_)
  idx <- which(yrs == yr_num)
  if (length(idx) > 0L) return(vals[idx[1]])
  stats::approx(x = yrs, y = vals, xout = yr_num, method = "linear")$y
}

fmt_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr_num)
  if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) return("-")
  viscount_fmt_pop(p)
}

fmt_site_peak <- function (e) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return("-")
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  i_pk <- which.max(vals)
  paste0(viscount_fmt_pop(vals[i_pk]), " (", as.integer(yrs[i_pk]), "AD)")
}

clean_site_name <- function (nm) {
  s <- as.character(nm)
  s <- gsub("#", "No. ", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s
}

iso_map <- c(
  Angola = "AGO",
  Benin = "BEN",
  `Burkina Faso` = "BFA",
  Cameroon = "CMR",
  `Central African Republic` = "CAF",
  `Democratic Republic of the Congo` = "COD",
  `Equatorial Guinea` = "GNQ",
  Gabon = "GAB",
  Gambia = "GMB",
  Ghana = "GHA",
  Guinea = "GIN",
  `Guinea-Bissau` = "GNB",
  `Ivory Coast` = "CIV",
  Liberia = "LBR",
  Mali = "MLI",
  Mauritania = "MRT",
  Namibia = "NAM",
  Nigeria = "NGA",
  `Republic of the Congo` = "COG",
  Senegal = "SEN",
  `Sierra Leone` = "SLE",
  `South Sudan` = "SSD",
  Togo = "TGO",
  Zambia = "ZMB"
)

classify_awe_zone <- function (e) {
  lat <- as.numeric(e$coords[[1]])
  lon <- as.numeric(e$coords[[2]])
  ctry <- as.character(e$country)
  if (ctry %in% c("Senegal", "Gambia", "Guinea-Bissau", "Mauritania", "Mali")) return(1L)
  if (identical(ctry, "Guinea")) {
    if (lat >= 10.90 && lon <= -12.0) return(1L)
    return(2L)
  }
  if (ctry %in% c("Sierra Leone", "Liberia")) return(2L)
  if (identical(ctry, "Ivory Coast")) {
    if (lon < -6.0) return(2L)
    return(3L)
  }
  if (identical(ctry, "Burkina Faso")) return(3L)
  if (identical(ctry, "Ghana")) {
    if ((lat >= 9.0 && lon >= -0.5) || (lat < 9.0 && lon >= 0.4 && lat >= 6.2)) return(4L)
    return(3L)
  }
  if (ctry %in% c("Togo", "Benin")) return(4L)
  if (identical(ctry, "Nigeria")) {
    if (lon < 3.35 && lat < 7.0) return(4L)
    if (lon >= 11.5) return(7L)
    if (lon >= 6.82 || (lat < 5.5 && lon >= 6.3) || (lon >= 6.78 && lat < 6.2)) return(6L)
    return(5L)
  }
  if (identical(ctry, "Equatorial Guinea")) {
    if (lat > 2.5) return(6L)
    return(8L)
  }
  if (identical(ctry, "Cameroon")) {
    if ((lat >= 5.8 && lon <= 10.3) || (lat < 4.5 && lon <= 9.5)) return(6L)
    return(7L)
  }
  if (ctry %in% c("Gabon", "Republic of the Congo")) return(8L)
  if (ctry %in% c("Central African Republic", "South Sudan")) return(11L)
  if (identical(ctry, "Namibia")) return(10L)
  if (identical(ctry, "Zambia")) {
    if (lat < -14.0 && lon < 26.0) return(10L)
    return(12L)
  }
  if (identical(ctry, "Angola")) {
    if (lat >= -5.7) return(8L)
    if (lat <= -10.5) return(10L)
    return(9L)
  }
  if (identical(ctry, "Democratic Republic of the Congo")) {
    if (lon >= 22.8 && lat <= -4.0) return(12L)
    if (lon < 13.3 && lat >= -5.85) return(8L)
    if (lat <= -4.8 && lon < 16.0) return(9L)
    if (lon <= 17.0 && lat <= -1.0) return(8L)
    return(11L)
  }
  return(11L)
}

zone_ids <- vapply(all_entries, classify_awe_zone, integer(1))
zone_entries <- lapply(1:12, function (z) {
  sub <- all_entries[zone_ids == z]
  pks <- vapply(sub, function (e) max(as.numeric(unlist(e$population))), numeric(1))
  sub[order(-pks, vapply(sub, function (e) e$name, character(1)))]
})

build_gazetteer_df <- function (sub_list) {
  rows <- lapply(sub_list, function (e) {
    iso_code <- unname(iso_map[as.character(e$country)])
    if (is.na(iso_code)) iso_code <- toupper(substr(as.character(e$country), 1L, 3L))
    loc_str <- paste0(
      iso_code,
      ": ",
      fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[1]]),
      ", ",
      fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[2]])
    )
    data.frame(
      Settlement = clean_site_name(e$name),
      Location = loc_str,
      `1500AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1500),
      `1700AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1700),
      `1800AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1800),
      `1850AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1850),
      `1880AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1880),
      Peak = fmt_site_peak(e),
      check.names = FALSE,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
  df <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rownames(df) <- NULL
  df
}

n_excluded <- as.integer(summary_cache$wave_saturation_stats$ledger_excluded)
n_candidates <- length(all_entries) + n_excluded
n_obs <- as.integer(summary_cache$observation_count)
n_countries <- length(summary_cache$countries)

bench_nums <- c(1500, 1700, 1800, 1850, 1880)
bench_keys <- as.character(bench_nums)
n_active <- setNames(
  vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) sum(vapply(all_entries, function (e) !is.na(interp_site_pop(e, yr)), logical(1))), integer(1)),
  bench_keys
)
```

# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles coordinates and dated population series for `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements across Atlantic West Africa, Equatorial Africa and Angola between 1500AD and 1885AD, encompassing `r viscount_fmt_number(n_obs, 0L)` archival observations across `r n_countries` modern countries. Screened from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_candidates, 0L)` candidate towns, royal capitals, European forts and market centres (`r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` excluded), the retained settlements span twelve historical sub-regions from Senegambia and Upper Guinea through Asante, Dahomey, Oyo-Yorubaland, Benin, the Niger Delta and Cameroon to Loango, Kongo, Angola, Kuba and the Luba-Lunda commonwealth. Active entries expand from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1500"]], 0L)` attested sites in 1500AD to `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1700"]], 0L)` in 1700AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1800"]], 0L)` in 1800AD and `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1850"]], 0L)` in 1850AD before consolidating at `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1880"]], 0L)` late precolonial towns in 1880AD, documenting urban dynamics from Mbanza Congo (52k), Benin City (52,8k) and Old Oyo (99,8k) to nineteenth-century Ibadan (200k), Abeokuta (100k) and Ilorin (85k).

# Background

Early modern urbanism across Atlantic Africa developed within starkly different political and ecological settings [@Green2015AfricanKingdoms]. Along the Senegambian savanna and Upper Guinea estuaries, compact royal capitals and Luso-African or French river entrepôts mediated millet, rice, gold and gum commerce [@Havik2007PortOfGeba; @Howard1900MandeIdentity]. Across the Akan forest, the Dahomey Gap and Yorubaland, walled city-states and agrarian capitals supported dense populations backed by yam farming, ironworking and Atlantic-era maize and cassava [@Kirkgreene2001ComparativeStudy; @Monroe2014DahomeySlavery; @Ogundiran2009OyoFrontier]. South of the Niger Delta across Loango, Kongo, Angola and the Luba-Lunda interior, royal capitals and Portuguese presídios punctuated lower-density woodland and highland savannas [@Thornton1977KongoDemography; @Ferreira2011TheSuppression; @Coloniales1920CongoRevue].

# Methodology

## Candidate Screening and Spatial Partition

Candidate entries were compiled from Portuguese Angolan presídio censuses [@Ferreira2011TheSuppression; @Curto2005ResistenciaEscravidao], French Senegalese communal registers, Gold Coast and Nigerian enumerations, traveller eyewitness reports and archaeological transect surveys [@AgbajeWilliam1990NewsAnd; @Monroe2014DahomeySlavery; @Law1977OyoEmpire]. From `r viscount_fmt_number(n_candidates, 0L)` candidates located inside the 7,03M km² domain clipped to geoBoundaries outlines [@Runfola2020GeoBoundaries], `r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` duplicate orthographies and non-settlement fragments were excluded, retaining `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` city-proper settlements across `r n_countries` countries. Every entry is mapped deterministically to one of the 12 historical sub-regions defined in the companion review.

## Population Assessment and Interpolation

All entries carry explicit city-proper population observations anchored to documented years rather than uniform caps or back-projections. Where primary archival or archaeological counts span multiple dates (such as Mbanza Congo from 1550AD to 1885AD or Luanda from 1580AD to 1885AD), Tables 1 to 12 report linearly interpolated values at five benchmark dates (1500AD, 1700AD, 1800AD, 1850AD and 1880AD) alongside each settlement's observed peak and peak year, marking periods outside a site's documented span with a hyphen (-).

# Testing and Validation

Across 299 spatially deduplicated settlements ($n = 299$), OLS rank-size regression on the upper 150 settlements yields a Pareto slope of $q = 0,81$ ($R^2 = 0,98$; Figure \ref{fig:settlements-rank}), matching a polycentric coastal-and-inland urban hierarchy rather than single-city primacy [@Ogundiran2009OyoFrontier; @AgbajeWilliam1990NewsAnd]. Typological screening confirms zero duplicate place-names at matching dates, zero unverified modern extrapolations and consistent alignment with historical foundation and abandonment dates [@Law1977OyoEmpire; @Thornton1977KongoDemography].

```{r fig3-ranksize, results='asis'}
viscount_figure(
  "figures/fig_03_rank_size.png",
  "Rank-size distribution across 299 spatially deduplicated settlements (top-150 OLS slope q = 0,81, R² = 0,98) and mean population densities of the ten densest sub-regions in 1880AD.",
  "fig:settlements-rank",
  arg3_options = list(max_height = "0.40\\textheight")
)
```

# Limitations

Three caveats apply to this settlement ledger. First, archival survival favours coastal enclaves and major royal capitals over dispersed interior villages, leaving inner Congo and Luba-Lunda with fewer individually dated towns than Senegambia or the Gulf of Guinea [@Thornton1977KongoDemography; @Coloniales1920CongoRevue]. Second, linear interpolation between dated observations cannot capture sudden unrecorded war shocks between benchmark observations [@Law1977OyoEmpire; @Monroe2014DahomeySlavery]. Third, the `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` entries measure urban and major market centres rather than total rural headcounts, which appear in the companion regional synthesis.

# Conclusion

Together, these `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed settlements document the shifting urban geography of Atlantic West Africa, Equatorial Africa and Angola from 1500AD to 1885AD. They capture early royal capitals such as Mbanza Congo, Benin City and Allada, the rise and collapse of Old Oyo, nineteenth-century Yoruba defensive agglomeration at Ibadan and Abeokuta, the maritime entrepôts of Luanda, Saint-Louis, Freetown and Lagos, and late precolonial caravan hubs across Luba-Lunda and Katanga.

## Regional Gazetteer Summary

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer-summary} sums the individually assessed settlement counts and combined interpolated urban populations across all twelve sub-regions at the five chapter benchmarks from 1500AD to 1880AD.

```{r tab-appendix-summary, results='asis'}
zone_names <- c(
  "1. Wolof States, Futa Jallon and Kaabu",
  "2. Sierra Leone, Grain Coast and Liberia",
  "3. Asante Empire, Fante and Gold Coast",
  "4. Kingdom of Dahomey, Allada and Ewe",
  "5. Oyo Empire, Yorubaland and Benin",
  "6. Niger Delta, Arochukwu and Cross River",
  "7. Bamum, Cameroon Grassfields and Biafra",
  "8. Loango, Teke-Makoko and Gabon",
  "9. Kongo, Ndongo, Matamba and Angola",
  "10. Ovimbundu, Benguela and S. Angola",
  "11. Kuba, Inner Congo and Ubangi",
  "12. Luba, Lunda and Kazembe"
)
sum_rows <- lapply(1:12, function (z) {
  sub <- zone_entries[[z]]
  sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
    vals <- vapply(sub, function (e) {
      p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
      if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
    }, numeric(1))
    viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
  }, character(1)), bench_keys)
  data.frame(
    `Subregion (Sites)` = paste0(zone_names[z], " (", viscount_fmt_number(length(sub), 0L), ")"),
    `1500AD` = sums[["1500"]],
    `1700AD` = sums[["1700"]],
    `1800AD` = sums[["1800"]],
    `1850AD` = sums[["1850"]],
    `1880AD` = sums[["1880"]],
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
tot_sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
  vals <- vapply(all_entries, function (e) {
    p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
    if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
  }, numeric(1))
  viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
}, character(1)), bench_keys)
tot_row <- data.frame(
  `Subregion (Sites)` = paste0("All Sub-Regions (", viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L), ")"),
  `1500AD` = tot_sums[["1500"]],
  `1700AD` = tot_sums[["1700"]],
  `1800AD` = tot_sums[["1800"]],
  `1850AD` = tot_sums[["1850"]],
  `1880AD` = tot_sums[["1880"]],
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_sum <- rbind(do.call(rbind, sum_rows), tot_row)
rownames(df_sum) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_sum,
  "Individually assessed settlement counts and combined interpolated urban populations across the twelve sub-regions from 1500AD to 1880AD.",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:gazetteer-summary")
)
```

# Footnotes

Settlement coordinates follow decimal degrees (latitude, longitude) formatted with European decimal commas in gazetteer tables. Settlements recorded under slightly variant historical spellings or overlapping port names (such as Freetown and Lagos) retain distinct entries where documented in separate historical series.
